442	    /// The arguments in the op's order — every required one read before an id is looked up,
443	    /// so a missing one is named as missing whatever the others hold — and the camera's masks
444	    /// when `focus` is left out.
445	    private func resolveLayout(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> LayoutCall {
446	        let document = try target(a)
447	        _ = try idArg(a, "camera")
448	        let layout = try requiredEnumArg(a, "layout", CameraLayoutKind.self)
449	        let at = try timeArg(a, "at", document)
450	        let camera = try clipArg(a, "camera", document)
451	        var screen: UInt32?
452	        if let raw = a["screen"], !(raw is NSNull) {
453	            screen = try clipArg(a, "screen", document).id
454	        }
455	        let focus = try pointArg(a, "focus")
456	        return LayoutCall(
457	            document: document, camera: camera.id, screen: screen, layout: layout,
458	            shape: try enumArg(a, "shape", CameraLayoutShape.self),
459	            corner: try enumArg(a, "corner", CameraLayoutCorner.self), at: at,
460	            duration: try optionalTimeArg(a, "duration", document),
461	            curve: try enumArg(a, "curve", Curve.self), focus: focus,
462	            nest: try boolArg(a, "nest"),
463	            through: try optionalTimeArg(a, "through", document),
464	            inputs: focus == nil ? CameraLayoutFocus.inputs(camera: camera.id, in: document) : nil,
465	            asked: document.project, scope: document.scope)
466	    }
467	
468	    /// Two finite numbers, `[x, y]`, or nil when absent or null.
469	    private func pointArg(_ a: [String: Any], _ key: String) throws -> (Double, Double)? {
470	        guard let raw = a[key], !(raw is NSNull) else { return nil }
471	        let numbers = (raw as? [Any])?.compactMap { value -> Double? in
472	            guard let number = value as? NSNumber,
473	                CFGetTypeID(number) != CFBooleanGetTypeID()
474	            else { return nil }
475	            return number.doubleValue
476	        }
477	        guard let numbers, numbers.count == 2, (raw as? [Any])?.count == 2,
478	            numbers.allSatisfy(\.isFinite)
479	        else {
480	            throw ToolError(message: "\(key) must be two numbers, [x, y].")
481	        }
482	        return (numbers[0], numbers[1])
483	    }

2	title: "Reframe a clip (agents)"
3	description: How an agent frames one clip on the canvas, from following a face, a pointer or whoever is talking to rescaling it from an older canvas.
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	An agent frames one clip on the current canvas with `reframe_clip`, say a landscape recording on a 1080 × 1920 canvas. [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/) and [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/) frame clips the same way, and this page is for when you want an agent to do it one clip at a time, with every choice in its hands.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  menu={['Clip ▸ Follow Subject…', 'File ▸ Make Vertical Version…']}
12	  tools={['reframe_clip', 'set_canvas', 'undo']}
13	  needs="Nothing to set up. Faces, people and salient regions are found on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
14	/>
15	
16	## Frame a clip
17	
18	An agent gives `reframe_clip` two things: the clip, and what to `follow`. Everything else is optional, and [Tools: framing and vertical](/mcp/tools-framing/) lists it all.
19	
20	The frame is worked out for the project's current canvas, so the agent sets the canvas first. Inside a [nest](/mcp/nests/), the nest's canvas is the canvas.
21	
22	A framing that would leave the clip exactly as it is changes nothing, and the agent is told the project is already in that state. There's no undo step for it.
23	
24	## Choose what to follow
25	
26	| `follow` | What the frame does | Analysis |
27	| --- | --- | --- |
28	| `subject` | Follows a face, else a person, else a salient region | Yes |
29	| `face`, `person`, `salient` | Follows only that kind | Yes |
30	| `cursor` | Follows a screen recording's recorded pointer | None, reads the cursor file |
31	| `speaker` | Cuts to whoever is talking in a wide shot | Yes, and the microphones' speech |
32	| `center` | Holds on the middle of the picture | None |
33	| `fit` | Shows the whole picture | None |
34	| `layout` | Re-lays camera layouts on this canvas | None |
35	| `keep` | Rescales the clip from an older canvas | None |
36	
37	The first four rows move the frame over time. The sheets don't offer all of these. **Clip ▸ Follow Subject…** has Subject, Faces, People, Salient Region and Center, **File ▸ Make Vertical Version…** adds Speaker, and Make Vertical uses `cursor`, `fit`, `layout` and `keep` by itself where a clip calls for them. See [What Make Vertical changes](/framing/vertical-what-changes/).
38	
39	### `subject`
40	
41	Follows a face. Where there's no face it follows a person, and where there's neither it follows a salient region, the part of the picture that draws the eye. This is **Subject** in [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/), and [How a followed frame moves](#how-a-followed-frame-moves) says what the frame does.
42	
43	### `face`, `person` and `salient`
44	
45	Each follows only that kind. Where there's none to follow, the frame behaves as it does when a subject is lost. These are **Faces**, **People** and **Salient Region** on the Follow Subject sheet.
46	
47	A clip whose media has a [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/) can't use `subject` or these three, because a recording with a cursor file follows its cursor, never faces.
48	
49	### `cursor`
50	
51	Follows a screen recording's recorded pointer, from its media's [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/). A screen recording made by Frame Job has one.
52	
53	- The frame sits on the pointer and moves only when the pointer strays more than 20 % of the frame's width, or 12 % of its height, from the middle.
54	- A click outside that area gets there in time: the move ends on the click's frame.
55	- The frame holds still while you type. A click during typing still moves it.
56	
57	It needs no analysis, so it never waits. The frame never shows the whole picture, so `where_empty` and `backdrop` do nothing here.
58	
59	If the cursor file is missing or won't open, the agent is told which file and why. The **Cursor** section of the Media tab has **Locate…** to point the media at a moved file.
60	
61	### `speaker`
62	
63	Frames a wide shot of two to four people on whoever is talking. Each person needs a microphone of their own, and the agent names those clips in `mics`.
64	
65	- **Who talks when** is read from the microphones exactly as [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) reads them with its default settings, so the two agree.
66	- **Whose face is whose** comes from matching each microphone to the face whose mouth moves while it talks. Faces are numbered 1, 2 and so on from left to right, and a face has to be in view for at least a quarter of the clip to count.
67	- **Each change of speaker** is a cut, held at least 2 s.
68	- **Two people talking at once** are framed together when they fit, and otherwise the frame stays on the one already framed.
69	- **While nobody talks**, the last speaker stays.
70	
71	**File ▸ Make Vertical Version…** has this as Follow **Speaker**, with the microphones and faces confirmed on the sheet. See [Follow the speaker in a vertical](/framing/follow-speaker/).
72	
73	When the mouths are too still or too small to read, Frame Job can't tell who is whose. The agent is told where each face is across the picture, for example "face 1 at 28 % across the picture, face 2 at 71 %". It then names each microphone's face in `mic_faces`, in the same order as `mics`, and calls again.
74	
75	Frame Job won't frame on the speaker when:
76	
77	| The problem | What to do |
78	| --- | --- |
79	| `mics` doesn't hold two to four clips, or names a clip twice | Name each microphone once |
80	| A microphone is the clip being framed, or has no sound from a media file | Use a clip of a sound file, or a camera's detached sound |
81	| A microphone's sound is off | Turn it on, or leave it out of `mics` |
82	| Two microphones are on one track | Give each its own track |
83	| `mic_faces` has the wrong count, a face 0, a face twice, or a number past the faces shown | Name one different face for each microphone |
84	| A microphone is still being measured | Try again in a moment. Frame Job measures loudness and speech when a file is added |
85	| A microphone has no speech over the clip | Leave it out, or check it's the right clip |
86	| The clip changes shot | Split it first with [Split at Shot Changes](/editing/split-at-shot-changes/) |
87	| Fewer faces show than there are microphones | Use fewer microphones, or a shot that shows everyone |
88	| Nobody speaks inside the clip | Frame the clip another way |
89	
90	`speaker` reads the microphones on what's open in the window, so a call addressed to a nest that isn't open stops and says to open it with `set_scope` first.
91	
92	### `center`
93	
94	Holds the frame on the middle of the picture for the whole clip. It needs no analysis, and it reads `zoom`.
95	
96	### `fit`
97	
98	Shows the whole picture for the whole clip, scaled to fit the canvas. It needs no analysis and doesn't read `zoom`. It has no menu choice of its own, but Make Vertical uses it for a recording whose cursor file can't be read.
99	
100	### `layout`
101	
102	Re-lays a camera clip's [camera layouts](/framing/camera-layouts/), and its screen's, on the current canvas, as Make Vertical Version does. The agent can name the camera or the screen, and both are re-laid.
103	
104	Each switch made on the old canvas, `from_width` × `from_height`, is recognised, to within 1 px and 0.001, and switched again here at the same time, length and curve. Without those two arguments the old canvas is taken to be the current one.
105	
106	- **Side by Side** becomes **Stacked** on a canvas taller than wide.
107	- The cut pieces of the recording take the new layout.
108	- Any zoom on them is re-based so it shows the same part of the picture.
109	
110	It reads no `zoom`, `where_empty`, `backdrop` or `replace`.
111	
112	Frame Job won't re-lay a clip with no camera layout, a clip laid out both as a camera and as a screen, a screen layout with no camera switch in front of it, or a switch edited by hand. The agent is told the clip and the action. For a clip with no layout it can use `subject`, `center`, `fit` or `keep`, and a clip it can't re-lay stays as placed.
113	
114	### `keep`
115	
116	Rescales the clip from the canvas it was placed on, `from_width` × `from_height`, to the current one, as `set_canvas` does with `rescale_clips`. Its position follows each axis's change and its scale follows the smaller of the two, and every position and scale its actions set moves with it. Each argument defaults to the current canvas's size, so with neither there's nothing to rescale.
117	
118	It needs no analysis and doesn't read `zoom`, `where_empty`, `backdrop` or `replace`.
119	
120	It works on every clip the other kinds turn down, as long as the clip has a picture. Make Vertical keeps titles, shapes and other clips this way.
121	
122	## How a followed frame moves
123	
124	With `subject`, `face`, `person` and `salient`, the frame:
125	
126	- eases onto the subject and moves only when the subject leaves the middle of the frame, so a speaker who sways stays put
127	- cuts with the picture at each shot change, landing on the first frame of the new shot
128	- holds for 1 s when the subject is lost, so a blink or a turned head changes nothing
129	- then follows someone else in the shot, or eases over 0.8 s to what `where_empty` says
130	- comes back once a subject has been in view for 0.6 s
131	- frames two people together when both fit in the frame
132	
133	`where_empty` is what the frame shows where there's nothing to follow: `fit`, the whole picture and the default, or `center`, the middle of the picture. These are **Show Whole** and **Center** on the Follow Subject sheet. A clip with nothing to follow anywhere in it shows this for its whole length.
134	
135	## Set how tight the frame is
136	
137	`zoom` is how tight the frame is, from 1 to 4. At 1, the default, the picture just covers the canvas. At 2 it's twice that scale.
138	
139	`center`, `subject`, `face`, `person`, `salient`, `cursor` and `speaker` read it. A value outside 1 to 4 stops the call whichever kind it asks for.
140	
141	## Put a blurred copy behind the clip
142	
143	Where the framing shows the whole picture, the canvas shows around it. Name a track behind the clip as `backdrop` and a blurred copy of the clip goes there for the clip's whole length. It's the copy **Clip ▸ Add Blurred Background** makes. See [Backgrounds](/canvas/backgrounds/).
144	
145	- With no `backdrop`, there's no copy.
146	- A copy is made only when the framing shows the whole picture somewhere: with `fit`, or with a followed clip that falls back to the whole picture.
147	- If the named track is locked, a matte, or busy over the clip, the copy goes on a new track at the back instead.
148	- A clip with speed actions keeps them on its copy, so the copy shows the same frames.
149	
150	## Written as ordinary edits
151	
152	The framing is written as the clip's position and scale, and one action per move, each of which you can change afterwards like any other [action](/motion/actions/). You'll see them on the [action lane](/motion/action-lane/).
153	
154	**Edit ▸ Undo Reframe Clip** takes the whole framing back in one step, and so does the agent's `undo`.
155	
156	## A clip that already has actions
157	
158	A clip keeps the actions it has. The framing is composed into them, so a zoom or pan the clip already makes still happens, inside the new framing, and a volume or speed action still does what it did.
159	
160	The framing's own moves go in the gaps between the clip's actions. A move that would overlap one is moved up to half a second earlier, or else made part of that action, along its curve.
161	
162	A shot change that falls inside an action cuts the action in three around the one-frame cut. A steady change of volume still sounds exactly as it did, and an eased one eases again on each side of the cut. A speed action, or one a trim left running past the clip's end, is never cut, and takes the framing's change across its length instead.
163	
164	### Start from the whole picture
165	
166	With `replace` set to true, the framing replaces the clip's own moves instead of working inside them. Every position and scale the clip's actions set is removed, the picture is fitted to the canvas, and then the clip is framed. Volume and everything else stay, and an action left with nothing is removed.
167	
168	The default is false. Every kind reads it but `keep` and `layout`. **Clip ▸ Follow Subject…** always starts from the whole picture this way, with a **Backgrounds** track as its `backdrop`, as one undo step named **Follow Subject**.
169	
170	## Which options each kind reads
171	
172	| `follow` | `zoom` | `where_empty` | `backdrop` | `replace` | `from_width`, `from_height` |
173	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
174	| `subject`, `face`, `person`, `salient` | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | No |
175	| `speaker` | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | No |
176	| `cursor` | Yes | No | No | Yes | No |
177	| `center` | Yes | No | No | Yes | No |
178	| `fit` | No | No | Yes | Yes | No |
179	| `layout` | No | No | No | No | Yes |
180	| `keep` | No | No | No | No | Yes |
181	
182	`mics` and `mic_faces` belong to `speaker` alone.
183	
184	## Waiting for analysis
185	
186	If the part of the file the clip plays hasn't been analysed, the tool analyses it and waits up to a minute. It looks at the clip's window with a second either side, for shots, faces and subjects, on your Mac. The answer says whether an analysis ran first.
187	
188	If a minute isn't enough, nothing changes. The answer says which files are still going and how much is covered, and the analysis carries on. The agent asks again to apply the framing.
189	
190	- `center`, `fit` and `keep` need no analysis, and `cursor` and `layout` read none.
191	- `speaker` also needs its microphones' loudness and speech, which Frame Job measures when a file is added.
192	- If the project or the open nest changes while the tool reads the analysis, nothing is framed and the agent is told to call again.
193	- If the analysis fails, nothing is framed and the agent is told which analysis and why.
194	- Stopping the [Assistant](/assistant/chat/) during the wait frames nothing.
195	
196	## When a clip can't be framed
197	
198	A clip that can't be framed is left as it was, and the agent gets a sentence saying why. Frame Job checks in this order and stops at the first one that applies.
199	
200	| The clip | Which kinds it stops | What still works |
201	| --- | --- | --- |
202	| A text, shape, graphic or adjustment clip | All but `keep` | `keep` |
203	| Has no picture, or a crop or scale leaves none | All | Nothing |
204	| A nest clip, then a still or image clip | `subject`, `face`, `person`, `salient`, `cursor`, `speaker` | `center`, `fit`, `keep` |
205	| Its media has no cursor file | `cursor` | `subject`, `center`, `fit`, `keep` |
206	| Its media has a cursor file | `subject`, `face`, `person`, `salient`, `speaker` | `cursor`, `center`, `fit`, `keep` |
207	| On a [matte track](/canvas/matte-tracks/), or cut by a matte | All but `keep` and `layout` | `keep` |
208	| Turned: a rotation, an action turning it, or a spin in its motion | All but `keep` and `layout` | `keep` |
209	| With a copy to make, a nest clip, or a `backdrop` track that isn't behind the clip's | Any kind that makes a copy | Leave `backdrop` out, or name a track further back |
210	| Analysis holds nothing for the part of the clip that plays, or no recorded pointer falls inside it | `subject`, `face`, `person`, `salient`, `cursor` | `center`, `fit`, `keep` |
211	
212	`layout` has [its own checks](#layout), and it skips the matte and turned rows. [`speaker`'s checks](#speaker) come after the turned clip.
213	
214	Before any of that, a call stops on a value it can't use: an unknown clip, track or microphone, or a `from_width` or `from_height` of 0.
215

223	title: "Copy pieces to another track (agents)"
224	description: How an agent builds a program from synced cameras with copy_pieces, and what it can do with switch_by_speaker that the sheet can't.
225	---
226	
227	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
228	
229	An agent can cut a multicam program more directly than the menus do. `copy_pieces` copies parts of a clip onto another track at the same times, and `switch_by_speaker` can preview a cut and use two values the sheet doesn't show. This page is for anyone driving Frame Job from an agent. The exact arguments and answers of each tool are in [Tools: multicam](/mcp/tools-multicam/).
230	
231	<AtAGlance
232	  where="No menu item of its own. Clip ▸ Switch Angle ▸ and Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker… write with it."
233	  tools={['copy_pieces', 'switch_by_speaker', 'switch_angle']}
234	  needs="Nothing. When there's only one microphone, faces are read on your Mac."
235	/>
236	
237	## Copy pieces of a clip
238	
239	`copy_pieces` takes the parts of one clip between the times you give and puts them on another track at the same times. It's what [Switch Angle](/multicam/switch-angle/) and [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) are built from.
240	
241	| Argument | What it does | Required |
242	| --- | --- | --- |
243	| `clip` | The clip to copy from. | Yes |
244	| `track` | The track the pieces land on. It must be free over every range. | Yes |
245	| `ranges` | The stretches to copy, as `[[from, to], …]` in project times, at least one pair. Times are in ticks, 600,000 a second. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/). | Yes |
246	| `video` | Turns each piece's picture on or off. | No. Default: the clip's own setting. |
247	| `audio` | Turns each piece's sound on or off. | No. Default: the clip's own setting. |
248	
249	The whole call is one undo step, **Copy Pieces**. It also takes `scope`, and inside a nest the times and tracks are the nest's own.
250	
251	### What a piece is
252	
253	Each piece is exactly what splitting the clip at both ends of the range would leave in the middle. It shows the same source frames at the same times, so a piece of a synced camera stays in sync. It keeps the clip's speed, speed ramp, reversal, a graphic's own timeline, its actions and its timed words.
254	
255	A piece gets a new id, and no transition and no link.
256	
257	### How ranges are read
258	
259	- Each range's ends snap to the frame grid.
260	- A pair written backwards is the same range.
261	- A range that's empty on the grid is skipped. If that leaves nothing, nothing changes.
262	- Ranges can touch, but they can't overlap.
263	
264	## Cut a whole program from the cameras
265	
266	An agent cuts a whole program with one `copy_pieces` per camera clip. Give the camera's clip, the program track, and every stretch where that camera is on screen. The pieces land at the times they came from, so they fall into place around each other.
267	
268	A range has to sit inside the one clip, so a camera that stopped and started needs a call for each of its clips. When the sound comes from separate microphones, pass `audio: false` so the pieces stay silent.
269	
270	To change one shot afterwards, use `switch_angle`, the agent's form of [Switch Angle](/multicam/switch-angle/). See [Tools: multicam](/mcp/tools-multicam/).
271	
272	## When a copy won't happen
273	
274	Nothing changes when one of these stops the copy. Frame Job checks them in this order and reports the first it meets:
275	
276	1. The clip is a nest. A piece of a nest would replay the nest from its first frame.
277	2. A range falls outside the clip.
278	3. Two ranges overlap.
279	4. The destination track is locked.
280	5. The destination track holds a clip over one of the ranges. The answer names that clip and where it starts and ends. The clip you're copying from counts, so a piece can't land on its own track over itself.
281	
282	A copy that would take the project past 4,096 clips also fails.
283	
284	## Switch by Speaker from an agent
285	
286	`switch_by_speaker` cuts a Program track from the selected cameras, with the same values as the [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) sheet and the same result, as one undo step. [Switch by Speaker settings](/multicam/switch-settings/) explains the values.
287	
288	- Run `sync_audio` first. It trusts where the clips sit and doesn't check that they're in sync.
289	- Set the clips with `set_selection`, because it reads the selected clips.
290	- Every argument is optional, including who's who, the range and the track to replace.
291	- A number outside its range is an error, where the sheet would pull it back into range.
292	
293	### Preview the cut
294	
295	Pass `apply: false` to see the shots without editing anything. The answer lists each shot's camera, start and end, how many edits it would make and how many clips it would add, and nothing in the project moves. It's the same work as a real run, so it stops for the same reasons.
296	
297	The answer says it wasn't applied and names no undo step, and it gives no Program track unless you named one. The default is `true`.
298	
299	### Values only an agent can set
300	
301	| Argument | What it does | Default | Range |
302	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
303	| `min_turn` | The shortest turn that cuts. A shorter turn, such as a quick reply, starts no shot. | 1 s | 0.2 to 10 s |
304	| `dominance_db` | How far one active microphone must lead every other to count alone. Below that lead, two active microphones are crosstalk. | 8 dB | 0 to 30 dB |
305	
306	### Check which mode ran
307	
308	Every answer has a `mode`, either `microphones` or `faces`.
309	
310	Faces mode is [cutting from one microphone](/multicam/one-microphone/). You get it by naming one microphone for two or more cameras, and it's the default when the selection holds exactly one microphone. In this mode:
311	
312	- The answer's `note` reads "Faces guess who is talking; check the cuts."
313	- `min_shot` is 3 s unless you give it.
314	- A camera you name as `wide` takes no part in deciding who's talking.
315	
316	### Waiting for faces
317	
318	Where the sheet would show the Analyzing sheet, the tool waits for the faces, for up to 60 seconds. Past that it stops with nothing switched, and what it found is kept. Call it again to continue.
319	
320	If the analysis fails or is stopped, or the project changes during the wait, nothing is switched either.
321	
322	### When Switch by Speaker won't run
323	
324	Nothing changes when a call is stopped. These are checked together, and the answer names every one that applies, so you can fix them in one go:
325	
326	- Under two cameras, or over nine. A camera here is a track holding a selected clip with a picture.
327	- A person without a microphone or without a camera.
328	- One microphone for two people, outside faces mode.
329	- A microphone still being analysed, or with no speech in the range.
330	- A camera whose faces are still being found, or that shows no face whose mouth can be read.
331	- A stretch no camera covers.
332	
333	These each stop the call on their own:
334	
335	- A faces analysis that failed, was stopped or ran past the wait.
336	- A project that changed during the wait.
337	- More clips than the project may hold. Raise `min_shot` to make fewer shots.
338	- A track named to replace that can't take the shots: it's locked, it holds a selected clip, it isn't in front of the cameras, it has nothing in the range, or it holds a clip that isn't a piece of a camera.
339	- A camera clip linked to its detached sound. Use [Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/) first.

3	/// `reframe_clip` (road map "creator-jobs" VR2a2 and VR2b1, spec §11 VR-26…VR-28):
4	/// the op tool whose `subjects` the app fills from the analysis cache. It mirrors
5	/// Clip ▸ Follow Subject… (VR2b2, spec §11 VR-29: this op with `replace: true` per
6	/// selected clip and a "Backgrounds" backdrop track); every refusal is the core's
7	/// sentence, and Swift copies none of VR-26's or VR-27's rules (`replace` is
8	/// passed through as the caller sent it). It reads no `UserDefaults` (AU-68 (f)).
9	///
10	/// **Runs on the SERVER thread** (`creatorOffMainTools`), in three hops:
11	/// - the first main hop resolves the arguments and TRIES the op with no
12	///   `subjects`, scoped, on the document's project without committing (as the
13	///   inspector's probe does). Only the core's "no subjects" refusal (VR-26's
14	///   tenth, LAST so every other one answers the trial) leads to the analysis;
15	///   an applied, identity or other refused trial goes straight to the last
16	///   hop;
17	/// - the wait is `split_at_shots`'s: a new lane owner and CJ-25's bound. Past
18	///   it the same requests are wanted again on that owner, held by
19	///   `FramingWant` until every one has ended or the document closes, and the
20	///   answer is `analyzing`, with no edit;
21	/// - the subjects are read off main (`FramingSubjects`), and the last main hop
22	///   refuses a changed project or scope, then applies one op as one undo step,
23	///   "Reframe Clip".
24	///
25	/// `follow: cursor` (VR5, spec §11 VR-50 (i)) never waits: after the trial's "no
26	/// subjects" the first hop finds the media's cursor file (`AutoZoom.cursorFiles`, its
27	/// sentences the refusal), and the file is opened and read off main
28	/// (`FramingCursor.read`) in place of the analysis; the answer's `cached` is true.
29	///
30	/// `follow: speaker` (VR6a, spec §11 VR-60 (c)) waits for the analysis as a following
31	/// kind does; its `mics` and `mic_faces` are passed through, a call addressed to a
32	/// container other than the open one is refused before the trial, and the last main
33	/// hop adds `turns` to the subjects (`FramingSpeaker.turns`, Switch by Speaker's reading
34	/// of the microphones, its refusals SW-24's).
35	extension AgentServer {
36	
37	    /// What the first main hop resolves.
38	    private struct FramingCall {
39	        let document: ProjectDocument
40	        let clip: UInt32
41	        let follow: FramingFollow
42	        let zoom: Double?
43	        let whereEmpty: FramingWhereEmpty?
44	        let fromWidth: UInt32?
45	        let fromHeight: UInt32?
46	        let backdrop: UInt32?
47	        let replace: Bool?
48	        let mics: [UInt32]?
49	        let micFaces: [UInt32]?
50	        /// The analysis to read, or nil when the trial needs none.
51	        let reading: FramingReading?
52	        /// The cursor file to read for `follow: cursor`, or nil.
53	        let cursor: CursorReading?
54	        let asked: ReelProject
55	        let scope: UInt32?
56	
57	        func op(subjects: [String: Any]?) -> ReelOp {
58	            .reframeClip(
59	                clip: clip, follow: follow, zoom: zoom, whereEmpty: whereEmpty,
60	                fromWidth: fromWidth, fromHeight: fromHeight, backdrop: backdrop,
61	                replace: replace, mics: mics, micFaces: micFaces, subjects: subjects)
62	        }
63	
64	        /// The same call reading `reading` or `cursor` instead.
65	        func with(reading: FramingReading?, cursor: CursorReading?) -> FramingCall {
66	            FramingCall(
67	                document: document, clip: clip, follow: follow, zoom: zoom,
68	                whereEmpty: whereEmpty, fromWidth: fromWidth, fromHeight: fromHeight,
69	                backdrop: backdrop, replace: replace, mics: mics, micFaces: micFaces,
70	                reading: reading, cursor: cursor, asked: asked, scope: scope)
71	        }
72	    }
73	
74	    /// The clip's media, its windows and its cursor file (VR-50 (i)).
75	    private struct CursorReading {
76	        let media: MediaSnapshot
77	        let windows: [ClosedRange<Ticks>]
78	        let files: [UInt32: URL]
79	    }
80	
81	    /// The clip's media, its windows, the cache folder and what is missing.
82	    private struct FramingReading {
83	        let media: MediaSnapshot
84	        let windows: [ClosedRange<Ticks>]
85	        let cacheDir: URL
86	        let requests: [AnalysisRequest]
87	    }
88	
89	    func reframeClip(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> String {
90	        let stop = AgentLane.shared.callCancel  // the assistant's Stop (spec §11 AI-16)
91	        guard !Thread.isMainThread else {
92	            throw ToolError(
93	                message: "reframe_clip must run on the server thread — its name is missing "
94	                    + "from AgentServer.creatorOffMainTools.")
95	        }
96	        let call = try onMain { try self.resolveFraming(a) }
97	        var subjects: [String: Any]?
98	        if let reading = call.reading {
99	            if !reading.requests.isEmpty,
100	                let analyzing = try waitForAnalysis(
101	                    reading.requests, document: call.document, stop: stop,
102	                    unmade: "nothing was framed",
103	                    note: { percent in
104	                        "Still analyzing the media of clip \(call.clip) (\(percent) %); call "
105	                            + "reframe_clip again to apply."
106	                    })
107	            {
108	                return analyzing
109	            }
110	            subjects = FramingSubjects.read(
111	                media: reading.media, windows: reading.windows, cacheDir: reading.cacheDir)
112	        }
113	        if let cursor = call.cursor {
114	            do {
115	                guard let track = try AutoZoom.readTracks(cursor.files)[cursor.media.id] else {
116	                    throw ToolError(message: "Media \(cursor.media.id)'s cursor file was not read.")
117	                }
118	                subjects = try FramingCursor.read(
119	                    track, media: cursor.media, windows: cursor.windows)
120	            } catch let error as ToolError {
121	                throw error
122	            } catch {
123	                throw ToolError(message: error.localizedDescription)
124	            }
125	        }
126	        let cached = call.reading?.requests.isEmpty ?? true
127	        return try onMain {
128	            let document = call.document
129	            guard document.project === call.asked, document.scope == call.scope else {
130	                throw ToolError(
131	                    message: "the project changed while reframe_clip read the clip's analysis, "
132	                        + "so nothing was framed. Call reframe_clip again.")
133	            }
134	            // VR-60 (c): who speaks when, read on this hop from the microphones' caches.
135	            var filled = subjects
136	            if call.follow == .speaker, filled != nil,
137	                let shown = document.editedProject.snapshot.clip(call.clip)
138	            {
139	                do {
140	                    filled?["turns"] = try FramingSpeaker.turns(
141	                        document: document, clip: shown, mics: call.mics ?? [])
142	                } catch let refusal as FramingSpeaker.Refusal {
143	                    throw ToolError(message: "reframe_clip was refused: " + refusal.sentence)
144	                }
145	            }
146	            return try self.editResult(
147	                document, FramingWant.actionName, [call.op(subjects: filled)],
148	                ["cached": cached])
149	        }
150	    }
151	
152	    /// Every argument in the op's order, the trial, and — only when the core
153	    /// answered "no subjects" — what the analysis must cover.
154	    private func resolveFraming(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> FramingCall {
155	        let document = try target(a)
156	        _ = try idArg(a, "clip")
157	        let follow = try requiredEnumArg(a, "follow", FramingFollow.self)
158	        let clip = try clipArg(a, "clip", document)
159	        var backdrop: UInt32?
160	        if let raw = a["backdrop"], !(raw is NSNull) {
161	            backdrop = try trackArg(a, "backdrop", document).id
162	        }
163	        let call = FramingCall(
164	            document: document, clip: clip.id, follow: follow, zoom: try doubleArg(a, "zoom"),
165	            whereEmpty: try enumArg(a, "where_empty", FramingWhereEmpty.self),
166	            fromWidth: try sideArg(a, "from_width"), fromHeight: try sideArg(a, "from_height"),
167	            backdrop: backdrop, replace: try boolArg(a, "replace"),
168	            mics: try numbersArg(a, "mics"), micFaces: try numbersArg(a, "mic_faces"),
169	            reading: nil, cursor: nil, asked: document.project, scope: document.scope)
170	        let scope = effectiveScope(document)
171	        if follow == .speaker, scope != document.scope {
172	            throw ToolError(
173	                message: "reframe_clip was refused: follow speaker reads its microphones on the "
174	                    + "open timeline; open that nest first with set_scope")
175	        }
176	        let trial: ReelEdit
177	        do {
178	            trial = try document.project.applying(call.op(subjects: nil).scoped(scope))
179	        } catch {
180	            throw ToolError(message: error.localizedDescription)
181	        }
182	        guard case .refused(let refusal) = trial,
183	            refusal.reason == FramingWant.noSubjects(clip.id)
184	        else { return call }
185	        let view = scope.flatMap { document.project.scoped($0) } ?? document.project
186	        guard let entry = FramingAnalysis.windows(clips: [clip.id], in: view).first,
187	            let media = view.snapshot.media(entry.media)
188	        else { return call }
189	        if follow == .cursor {
190	            // VR-50 (i): the cursor file in place of the analysis; never a wait.
191	            guard let shown = view.snapshot.clip(clip.id) else { return call }
192	            let files: [UInt32: URL]
193	            do {
194	                files = try AutoZoom.cursorFiles([shown], in: view.snapshot)
195	            } catch {
196	                throw ToolError(message: error.localizedDescription)
197	            }
198	            return call.with(
199	                reading: nil,
200	                cursor: CursorReading(media: media, windows: entry.windows, files: files))
201	        }
202	        guard let cacheDir = document.cacheDirectory else {
203	            throw ToolError(message: ProjectDocument.AnalysisRequestError.noCache.localizedDescription)
204	        }
205	        let requests: [AnalysisRequest]
206	        do {

220	    func numbersArg(_ a: [String: Any], _ key: String) throws -> [UInt32]? {
221	        guard let raw = a[key], !(raw is NSNull) else { return nil }
222	        guard let list = raw as? [Any] else {
223	            throw ToolError(message: "\(key) must be a list of whole numbers.")
224	        }
225	        return try list.map { value in
226	            guard let number = value as? NSNumber, CFGetTypeID(number) != CFBooleanGetTypeID(),
227	                let n = Self.whole(number), n >= 0, n <= Int(UInt32.max)
228	            else { throw ToolError(message: "\(key) must be a list of whole numbers.") }
229	            return UInt32(n)

236	        guard let value = try intArg(a, key) else { return nil }
237	        guard value >= 0, value <= Int(UInt32.max) else {

243	    /// Wants the requests (non-empty) under an owner of the call's own and
244	    /// waits up to CJ-25's bound: nil once every one landed; past the bound
245	    /// the `analyzing` answer with `note(percent)`, the want held
246	    /// (`FramingWant`); a failure or a Stop throws naming the kind and the
247	    /// media, a Stop saying "so <unmade>.". `reframe_clip`'s and
248	    /// `make_vertical_version`'s wait (spec §11 VR-28, VR-37).
249	    func waitForAnalysis(
250	        _ requests: [AnalysisRequest], document: ProjectDocument, stop: AgentCallCancel?,
251	        unmade: String, note: @escaping (Int) -> String
252	    ) throws -> String? {
253	        let lane = AnalysisLane.shared
254	        let owner = lane.newOwner()
255	        lane.want(
256	            requests, owner: owner,
257	            alive: { document.isOpenForAnalysis && !(stop?.isCancelled ?? false) },
258	            settled: { document.packageContentsDidChangeOnDisk() })
259	        let outcome = lane.wait(
260	            for: requests, owner: owner,
261	            deadline: Date().addingTimeInterval(AnalysisLane.callWaitLimit),
262	            cancelled: { stop?.isCancelled ?? false })
263	        let open = requests.first { lane.run(of: $0)?.outcome != .landed } ?? requests[0]
264	        let named = "The \(open.kind.rawValue) analysis of media \(open.media.id)"
265	        switch outcome {
266	        case .landed:
267	            lane.release(owner: owner)
268	            return nil
269	        case .failed(let why):
270	            lane.release(owner: owner)
271	            throw ToolError(message: "\(named) failed: \(why).")
272	        case .cancelled:
273	            lane.release(owner: owner)
274	            throw ToolError(
275	                message: "\(named) was stopped before it finished, so \(unmade).")
276	        case .timedOut:
277	            let hold = FramingWant(requests: requests)
278	            lane.want(
279	                requests, owner: owner,
280	                alive: { document.isOpenForAnalysis && !hold.done },
281	                settled: {
282	                    hold.settle()
283	                    document.packageContentsDidChangeOnDisk()
284	                })
285	            return try onMain {
286	                let covered = FramingWant.covered(requests)
287	                let media = FramingWant.notLanded(requests)
288	                let percent = Int((covered * 100).rounded())
289	                return try self.jsonResult([
290	                    "ok": true,
291	                    "analyzing": ["media": media.map { Int($0) }, "covered": covered],
292	                    "note": note(percent),
293	                    "project": self.summary(document),
294	                ])
295	            }
296	        }
297	    }
298	}

300	/// The want `reframe_clip` leaves held past CJ-25's bound (spec §11 VR-28):
301	/// done once every request has ended, which `settled` marks, so the lane
302	/// drops the owner at its next poll; the owner is never released, so the
303	/// jobs run on after the call has answered. Its own `NSLock`, never the
304	/// lane's: `alive` is asked under the lane's lock.
305	final class FramingWant: @unchecked Sendable {
306	    /// The undo step's name.
307	    static let actionName = "Reframe Clip"
308	
309	    /// VR-26's tenth refusal, the one sentence a trial waits for; built as
310	    /// `core/src/edit_reframe.rs`'s `no_subjects` builds it, and pinned by
311	    /// `core/tests/reframe_clip.rs`.
312	    static func noSubjects(_ clip: UInt32) -> String {
313	        "clip \(clip) has no subjects to follow; analyze it first"
314	    }
315	
316	    private let lock = NSLock()
317	    private var ended = false
318	    private let requests: [AnalysisRequest]
319	
320	    init(requests: [AnalysisRequest]) {
321	        self.requests = requests
322	    }
323	
324	    var done: Bool {
325	        lock.lock()
326	        defer { lock.unlock() }
327	        return ended
328	    }
329	
330	    /// Main thread, from the owner's `settled`: done once every request's
331	    /// run has an outcome.
332	    func settle() {
333	        let lane = AnalysisLane.shared
334	        let all = requests.allSatisfy { lane.run(of: $0)?.outcome != nil }
335	        guard all else { return }
336	        lock.lock()
337	        ended = true
338	        lock.unlock()
339	    }
340	
341	    /// The share of the requests' missing indices their kinds' markers now
342	    /// cover (`AnalysisStore.coveredCount`), rounded to 2 decimals.
343	    static func covered(_ requests: [AnalysisRequest]) -> Double {
344	        var total = 0
345	        var held = 0
346	        for request in requests {
347	            let marker = AnalysisStore.readMarker(
348	                request.kind, media: request.media.id, in: request.cacheDir)
349	            let ranges = marker.map { $0.answers(for: request.stamp) ? $0.ranges : [] } ?? []
350	            for range in request.ranges {
351	                total += range.count
352	                held += AnalysisStore.coveredCount(range, covered: ranges)
353	            }
354	        }
355	        guard total > 0 else { return 1 }
356	        return (Double(held) / Double(total) * 100).rounded() / 100
357	    }
358	
359	    /// The media whose requests have not all landed, in request order.
360	    static func notLanded(_ requests: [AnalysisRequest]) -> [UInt32] {
361	        var media: [UInt32] = []
362	        for request in requests where AnalysisLane.shared.run(of: request)?.outcome != .landed {
363	            if !media.contains(request.media.id) { media.append(request.media.id) }
364	        }
365	        return media
366	    }
367	}

370	/// `switch_layout` (road map "creator-jobs" CO6, spec §11 CO-60…CO-66),
371	/// mirroring Clip ▸ Camera Layout ▸ (`switchCameraLayout` in
372	/// `EditorViewController+Layout.swift`, which sends this op at the playhead
373	/// with `duration` and `curve` left to the core): one op, one undo step
374	/// "Camera Layout", every refusal the core's sentence. Since CO7 (spec §11
375	/// CO-70) an omitted or null `focus` is filled from the camera clip's cached
376	/// person masks, as the menu and the Picture sub-tab's Layout section fill
377	/// it, and the answer carries the `focus` sent.
378	extension AgentServer {
379	
380	    /// What the first main-thread hop resolves.
381	    private struct LayoutCall {
382	        let document: ProjectDocument
383	        let camera: UInt32
384	        let screen: UInt32?
385	        let layout: CameraLayoutKind
386	        let shape: CameraLayoutShape?
387	        let corner: CameraLayoutCorner?
388	        let at: Ticks
389	        let duration: Ticks?
390	        let curve: Curve?
391	        let focus: (Double, Double)?
392	        let nest: Bool?
393	        let through: Ticks?
394	        /// The masks to fill `focus` from, when the caller left it out.
395	        let inputs: CameraLayoutFocus.Inputs?
396	        let asked: ReelProject
397	        let scope: UInt32?
398	
399	        func op(focus: (Double, Double)?) -> ReelOp {
400	            .switchLayout(
401	                camera: camera, screen: screen, layout: layout, shape: shape, corner: corner,
402	                at: at, duration: duration, curve: curve, focus: focus, nest: nest,
403	                through: through)
404	        }
405	    }
406	
407	    /// **Runs on the SERVER thread** (`creatorOffMainTools`): one main hop resolves the
408	    /// arguments and the camera's cached masks, the centroid is read here, and a last main hop
409	    /// refuses when the project or the scope changed meanwhile and applies as one undo step.
410	    func switchLayout(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> String {
411	        guard !Thread.isMainThread else {
412	            throw ToolError(
413	                message: "switch_layout must run on the server thread — its name is missing "
414	                    + "from AgentServer.creatorOffMainTools.")
415	        }
416	        let call = try onMain { try self.resolveLayout(a) }
417	        let filled = call.inputs.flatMap { CameraLayoutFocus.focus($0) }
418	        return try onMain {
419	            let document = call.document
420	            guard document.project === call.asked, document.scope == call.scope else {
421	                throw ToolError(
422	                    message: "the project changed while switch_layout read the camera's person "
423	                        + "masks, so nothing was laid out. Call switch_layout again.")
424	            }
425	            var focus = call.focus ?? filled
426	            // A filled focus is in the camera media's pixels: never sent to the nest clip
427	            // that `nest: true` puts in the camera's place (CO-70).
428	            if call.focus == nil, filled != nil, call.nest == true,
429	                let nested = self.addressed([call.op(focus: filled)], document).first,
430	                !CameraLayoutCommand.keepsFocus(
431	                    nested: nested, camera: call.camera, document: document)
432	            {
433	                focus = nil
434	            }
435	            let answer: Any = focus.map { [$0.0, $0.1] } ?? NSNull()
436	            return try self.editResult(
437	                document, CameraLayoutCommand.actionName, [call.op(focus: focus)],
438	                ["focus": answer])
439	        }
440	    }
441	
442	    /// The arguments in the op's order — every required one read before an id is looked up,
443	    /// so a missing one is named as missing whatever the others hold — and the camera's masks
444	    /// when `focus` is left out.
445	    private func resolveLayout(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> LayoutCall {
446	        let document = try target(a)
447	        _ = try idArg(a, "camera")
448	        let layout = try requiredEnumArg(a, "layout", CameraLayoutKind.self)
449	        let at = try timeArg(a, "at", document)
450	        let camera = try clipArg(a, "camera", document)
451	        var screen: UInt32?
452	        if let raw = a["screen"], !(raw is NSNull) {
453	            screen = try clipArg(a, "screen", document).id
454	        }
455	        let focus = try pointArg(a, "focus")
456	        return LayoutCall(
457	            document: document, camera: camera.id, screen: screen, layout: layout,
458	            shape: try enumArg(a, "shape", CameraLayoutShape.self),
459	            corner: try enumArg(a, "corner", CameraLayoutCorner.self), at: at,
460	            duration: try optionalTimeArg(a, "duration", document),
461	            curve: try enumArg(a, "curve", Curve.self), focus: focus,
462	            nest: try boolArg(a, "nest"),
463	            through: try optionalTimeArg(a, "through", document),
464	            inputs: focus == nil ? CameraLayoutFocus.inputs(camera: camera.id, in: document) : nil,
465	            asked: document.project, scope: document.scope)
466	    }
467	
468	    /// Two finite numbers, `[x, y]`, or nil when absent or null.
469	    private func pointArg(_ a: [String: Any], _ key: String) throws -> (Double, Double)? {
470	        guard let raw = a[key], !(raw is NSNull) else { return nil }
471	        let numbers = (raw as? [Any])?.compactMap { value -> Double? in
472	            guard let number = value as? NSNumber,
473	                CFGetTypeID(number) != CFBooleanGetTypeID()
474	            else { return nil }
475	            return number.doubleValue
476	        }
477	        guard let numbers, numbers.count == 2, (raw as? [Any])?.count == 2,
478	            numbers.allSatisfy(\.isFinite)
479	        else {
480	            throw ToolError(message: "\(key) must be two numbers, [x, y].")
481	        }
482	        return (numbers[0], numbers[1])
483	    }
484	}

487	/// `make_vertical_version` (spec §11 VR-36, VR-37; road map "creator-jobs" VR3a): the project's
488	/// 9:16, 4:5 or 1:1 version made by `VerticalVersion.plan`, opened as a copy through
489	/// `ProjectDocument.verticalCopy` (the default; saved at `path` when given) or, with
490	/// `copy: false`, applied to the addressed project in place as one undo step "Make Vertical".
491	/// Its UI path is File ▸ Make Vertical Version… (road map creator-jobs VR3b, spec §11 VR-39:
492	/// `EditorViewController+VerticalVersion.swift` and `VerticalVersionSheetController.swift`). It
493	/// never asks the person and reads no `UserDefaults`.
494	///
495	/// **Runs on the SERVER thread** (`creatorOffMainTools`), in hops:
496	/// - the first main hop resolves and refuses in VR-36's order, runs a DRY plan with no
497	///   subjects (so the core's own error for a bad argument is answered before any analysis is
498	///   asked for) and, for a following kind, asks `FramingAnalysis.requests` on the SOURCE over
499	///   the media pictures whose file is present (VR-37);
500	/// - the wait is `reframe_clip`'s (`waitForAnalysis`); past CJ-25's bound the answer is
501	///   `analyzing` and nothing is made; the subjects are read off main from the source's cache;
502	/// - the last main hop refuses a changed project or scope, plans on the current handle and
503	///   applies in place or opens the copy; with `path` the copy is saved on the server thread.

507	/// (`FramingCursor.subjects`), and the plan follows it with `replace: true` (VR-52).

510	/// analyses as a following kind does, and frames each speaker clip (`VerticalVersion.speakerClips`)
511	/// on whoever is talking: the last main hop fills their turns (`VerticalVersion.withTurns`,
512	/// Switch by Speaker's reading), a `FramingSpeaker.Refusal` refusing the call, and the answer
513	/// carries `speaker`. Its UI path is the sheet's Follow Speaker.
514	extension AgentServer {
515	
516	    /// What the first main hop resolves.
517	    private struct VerticalCall {
518	        let document: ProjectDocument
519	        let settings: VerticalSettings
520	        let copy: Bool
521	        let url: URL?
522	        /// Media pictures whose media file is missing (kept, not followed).
523	        let missing: Set<UInt32>
524	        /// The media pictures whose subjects are read: the following kinds' only.
525	        let targets: [UInt32]
526	        /// The media pictures whose cursor is read (VR-51): the following kinds' only.
527	        let cursor: [UInt32]
528	        let requests: [AnalysisRequest]
529	        let cacheDir: URL?
530	        let asked: ReelProject
531	        let scope: UInt32?
532	    }

534	    /// The last main hop's answer: in place, the finished answer; a copy, the document.
535	    private enum VerticalOutcome {
536	        case applied(String)
537	        case copied(
538	            (
539	                document: ProjectDocument, carried: DerivedCarry.Report,
540	                templates: VerticalVersion.TemplateReport

544	    func makeVerticalVersion(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> String {
545	        let stop = AgentLane.shared.callCancel  // the assistant's Stop (spec §11 AI-16)
546	        guard !Thread.isMainThread else {

548	                message: "make_vertical_version must run on the server thread — its name is "
549	                    + "missing from AgentServer.creatorOffMainTools.")
550	        }
551	        let call = try onMain { try self.resolveVertical(a) }
552	        var subjects: [UInt32: [String: Any]] = [:]
553	        if !call.requests.isEmpty {
554	            let clips = call.targets.count
555	            if let analyzing = try waitForAnalysis(
556	                call.requests, document: call.document, stop: stop, unmade: "nothing was made",

570	        let outcome: VerticalOutcome = try onMain {
571	            let document = call.document
572	            guard document.project === call.asked, document.scope == call.scope else {

658	    private func resolveVertical(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> VerticalCall {
659	        let document = try target(a)
660	        let shape = try requiredEnumArg(a, "shape", VerticalShape.self)
661	        var follow = FramingFollow.subject
662	        if let raw = try stringArg(a, "follow") {
663	            guard let kind = FramingFollow(rawValue: raw), VerticalVersion.follows.contains(kind)
664	            else {

667	                        + "not \(raw).")
668	            }
669	            follow = kind
670	        }
671	        let zoom = try doubleArg(a, "zoom") ?? 1
672	        let whereEmpty = try enumArg(a, "where_empty", FramingWhereEmpty.self) ?? .fit
673	        let copy = try boolArg(a, "copy") ?? true
674	        let captions = try boolArg(a, "captions") ?? true
675	        let path = try stringArg(a, "path")
676	        guard document.scope == nil else {
677	            throw ToolError(
678	                message: "make_vertical_version works on the top-level timeline: set_scope with "
679	                    + "no nest first.")
680	        }
681	        if path != nil, !copy {
682	            throw ToolError(
683	                message: "make_vertical_version writes path only for a copy: drop path, or copy.")
684	        }
685	        let url = path.map {
686	            Self.destinationURL($0, extension: ProjectDocument.projectFileExtension)
687	        }
688	        if let url {
689	            try refuseHeldPath(url, except: nil, tool: "make_vertical_version")

691	                throw ToolError(
692	                    message: "\(url.path) already exists, so make_vertical_version did not "
693	                        + "write there: pass a new path.")
694	            }
695	        }
696	        let project = document.project
697	        let canvas = project.snapshot.canvas
698	        let size = shape.size(from: canvas)
699	        guard size.width != canvas.width || size.height != canvas.height else {
700	            throw ToolError(
701	                message: "the canvas is already \(canvas.width) × \(canvas.height), so there is "
702	                    + "no \(shape.rawValue) version to make.")
703	        }
704	        do {
705	            if case .refused(let why) = try VerticalVersion.opening(
706	                project, width: size.width, height: size.height)
707	            {
708	                throw ToolError(message: why)
709	            }
710	        } catch let error as ToolError {
711	            throw error
712	        } catch {
713	            throw ToolError(message: error.localizedDescription)
714	        }
715	        // VR-64 (a), (e): the microphones, read only with speaker.
716	        var mics: [UInt32] = []
717	        var micFaces: [UInt32]?
718	        if follow == .speaker {
719	            guard let given = try numbersArg(a, "mics"), !given.isEmpty else {
720	                throw ToolError(
721	                    message: "make_vertical_version's follow speaker needs mics: two to four "
722	                        + "clips, one on each microphone's track.")
723	            }
724	            for id in given { _ = try clipArg(["clip": Int(id)], "clip", document) }
725	            mics = given
726	            micFaces = try numbersArg(a, "mic_faces")
727	        }
728	        let settings = VerticalSettings(
729	            shape: shape, follow: follow, zoom: zoom, whereEmpty: whereEmpty, captions: captions,
730	            mics: mics, micFaces: micFaces)
731	        let (present, missing, cursor) = VerticalVersion.analysisTargets(
732	            project, urls: document.mediaURLs())
733	        if follow == .speaker,
734	            VerticalVersion.speakerClips(project, settings: settings, missing: missing).isEmpty
735	        {
736	            throw ToolError(message: VerticalVersion.noSpeakerClip)
737	        }
738	        // The dry plan: the core's error for a bad argument, before any analysis. Its
739	        // refusal and its plan are discarded.

2	title: "Reframe a clip (agents)"
3	description: How an agent frames one clip on the canvas, from following a face, a pointer or whoever is talking to rescaling it from an older canvas.
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	An agent frames one clip on the current canvas with `reframe_clip`, say a landscape recording on a 1080 × 1920 canvas. [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/) and [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/) frame clips the same way, and this page is for when you want an agent to do it one clip at a time, with every choice in its hands.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  menu={['Clip ▸ Follow Subject…', 'File ▸ Make Vertical Version…']}
12	  tools={['reframe_clip', 'set_canvas', 'undo']}
13	  needs="Nothing to set up. Faces, people and salient regions are found on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
14	/>
15	
16	## Frame a clip
17	
18	An agent gives `reframe_clip` two things: the clip, and what to `follow`. Everything else is optional, and [Tools: framing and vertical](/mcp/tools-framing/) lists it all.
19	
20	The frame is worked out for the project's current canvas, so the agent sets the canvas first. Inside a [nest](/mcp/nests/), the nest's canvas is the canvas.
21	
22	A framing that would leave the clip exactly as it is changes nothing, and the agent is told the project is already in that state. There's no undo step for it.
23	
24	## Choose what to follow
25	
26	| `follow` | What the frame does | Analysis |
27	| --- | --- | --- |
28	| `subject` | Follows a face, else a person, else a salient region | Yes |
29	| `face`, `person`, `salient` | Follows only that kind | Yes |
30	| `cursor` | Follows a screen recording's recorded pointer | None, reads the cursor file |
31	| `speaker` | Cuts to whoever is talking in a wide shot | Yes, and the microphones' speech |
32	| `center` | Holds on the middle of the picture | None |
33	| `fit` | Shows the whole picture | None |
34	| `layout` | Re-lays camera layouts on this canvas | None |
35	| `keep` | Rescales the clip from an older canvas | None |
36	
37	The first four rows move the frame over time. The sheets don't offer all of these. **Clip ▸ Follow Subject…** has Subject, Faces, People, Salient Region and Center, **File ▸ Make Vertical Version…** adds Speaker, and Make Vertical uses `cursor`, `fit`, `layout` and `keep` by itself where a clip calls for them. See [What Make Vertical changes](/framing/vertical-what-changes/).
38	
39	### `subject`
40	
41	Follows a face. Where there's no face it follows a person, and where there's neither it follows a salient region, the part of the picture that draws the eye. This is **Subject** in [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/), and [How a followed frame moves](#how-a-followed-frame-moves) says what the frame does.
42	
43	### `face`, `person` and `salient`
44	
45	Each follows only that kind. Where there's none to follow, the frame behaves as it does when a subject is lost. These are **Faces**, **People** and **Salient Region** on the Follow Subject sheet.
46	
47	A clip whose media has a [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/) can't use `subject` or these three, because a recording with a cursor file follows its cursor, never faces.
48	
49	### `cursor`
50	
51	Follows a screen recording's recorded pointer, from its media's [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/). A screen recording made by Frame Job has one.
52	
53	- The frame sits on the pointer and moves only when the pointer strays more than 20 % of the frame's width, or 12 % of its height, from the middle.
54	- A click outside that area gets there in time: the move ends on the click's frame.
55	- The frame holds still while you type. A click during typing still moves it.
56	
57	It needs no analysis, so it never waits. The frame never shows the whole picture, so `where_empty` and `backdrop` do nothing here.
58	
59	If the cursor file is missing or won't open, the agent is told which file and why. The **Cursor** section of the Media tab has **Locate…** to point the media at a moved file.
60	
61	### `speaker`
62	
63	Frames a wide shot of two to four people on whoever is talking. Each person needs a microphone of their own, and the agent names those clips in `mics`.
64	
65	- **Who talks when** is read from the microphones exactly as [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) reads them with its default settings, so the two agree.
66	- **Whose face is whose** comes from matching each microphone to the face whose mouth moves while it talks. Faces are numbered 1, 2 and so on from left to right, and a face has to be in view for at least a quarter of the clip to count.
67	- **Each change of speaker** is a cut, held at least 2 s.
68	- **Two people talking at once** are framed together when they fit, and otherwise the frame stays on the one already framed.
69	- **While nobody talks**, the last speaker stays.
70	
71	**File ▸ Make Vertical Version…** has this as Follow **Speaker**, with the microphones and faces confirmed on the sheet. See [Follow the speaker in a vertical](/framing/follow-speaker/).
72	
73	When the mouths are too still or too small to read, Frame Job can't tell who is whose. The agent is told where each face is across the picture, for example "face 1 at 28 % across the picture, face 2 at 71 %". It then names each microphone's face in `mic_faces`, in the same order as `mics`, and calls again.
74	
75	Frame Job won't frame on the speaker when:
76	
77	| The problem | What to do |
78	| --- | --- |
79	| `mics` doesn't hold two to four clips, or names a clip twice | Name each microphone once |
80	| A microphone is the clip being framed, or has no sound from a media file | Use a clip of a sound file, or a camera's detached sound |
81	| A microphone's sound is off | Turn it on, or leave it out of `mics` |
82	| Two microphones are on one track | Give each its own track |
83	| `mic_faces` has the wrong count, a face 0, a face twice, or a number past the faces shown | Name one different face for each microphone |
84	| A microphone is still being measured | Try again in a moment. Frame Job measures loudness and speech when a file is added |
85	| A microphone has no speech over the clip | Leave it out, or check it's the right clip |
86	| The clip changes shot | Split it first with [Split at Shot Changes](/editing/split-at-shot-changes/) |
87	| Fewer faces show than there are microphones | Use fewer microphones, or a shot that shows everyone |
88	| Nobody speaks inside the clip | Frame the clip another way |
89	
90	`speaker` reads the microphones on what's open in the window, so a call addressed to a nest that isn't open stops and says to open it with `set_scope` first.
91	
92	### `center`
93	
94	Holds the frame on the middle of the picture for the whole clip. It needs no analysis, and it reads `zoom`.
95	
96	### `fit`
97	
98	Shows the whole picture for the whole clip, scaled to fit the canvas. It needs no analysis and doesn't read `zoom`. It has no menu choice of its own, but Make Vertical uses it for a recording whose cursor file can't be read.
99	
100	### `layout`
101	
102	Re-lays a camera clip's [camera layouts](/framing/camera-layouts/), and its screen's, on the current canvas, as Make Vertical Version does. The agent can name the camera or the screen, and both are re-laid.
103	
104	Each switch made on the old canvas, `from_width` × `from_height`, is recognised, to within 1 px and 0.001, and switched again here at the same time, length and curve. Without those two arguments the old canvas is taken to be the current one.
105	
106	- **Side by Side** becomes **Stacked** on a canvas taller than wide.
107	- The cut pieces of the recording take the new layout.
108	- Any zoom on them is re-based so it shows the same part of the picture.
109	
110	It reads no `zoom`, `where_empty`, `backdrop` or `replace`.
111	
112	Frame Job won't re-lay a clip with no camera layout, a clip laid out both as a camera and as a screen, a screen layout with no camera switch in front of it, or a switch edited by hand. The agent is told the clip and the action. For a clip with no layout it can use `subject`, `center`, `fit` or `keep`, and a clip it can't re-lay stays as placed.
113	
114	### `keep`
115	
116	Rescales the clip from the canvas it was placed on, `from_width` × `from_height`, to the current one, as `set_canvas` does with `rescale_clips`. Its position follows each axis's change and its scale follows the smaller of the two, and every position and scale its actions set moves with it. Each argument defaults to the current canvas's size, so with neither there's nothing to rescale.
117	
118	It needs no analysis and doesn't read `zoom`, `where_empty`, `backdrop` or `replace`.
119	
120	It works on every clip the other kinds turn down, as long as the clip has a picture. Make Vertical keeps titles, shapes and other clips this way.
121	
122	## How a followed frame moves
123	
124	With `subject`, `face`, `person` and `salient`, the frame:
125	
126	- eases onto the subject and moves only when the subject leaves the middle of the frame, so a speaker who sways stays put
127	- cuts with the picture at each shot change, landing on the first frame of the new shot
128	- holds for 1 s when the subject is lost, so a blink or a turned head changes nothing
129	- then follows someone else in the shot, or eases over 0.8 s to what `where_empty` says
130	- comes back once a subject has been in view for 0.6 s
131	- frames two people together when both fit in the frame
132	
133	`where_empty` is what the frame shows where there's nothing to follow: `fit`, the whole picture and the default, or `center`, the middle of the picture. These are **Show Whole** and **Center** on the Follow Subject sheet. A clip with nothing to follow anywhere in it shows this for its whole length.
134	
135	## Set how tight the frame is
136	
137	`zoom` is how tight the frame is, from 1 to 4. At 1, the default, the picture just covers the canvas. At 2 it's twice that scale.
138	
139	`center`, `subject`, `face`, `person`, `salient`, `cursor` and `speaker` read it. A value outside 1 to 4 stops the call whichever kind it asks for.
140	
141	## Put a blurred copy behind the clip
142	
143	Where the framing shows the whole picture, the canvas shows around it. Name a track behind the clip as `backdrop` and a blurred copy of the clip goes there for the clip's whole length. It's the copy **Clip ▸ Add Blurred Background** makes. See [Backgrounds](/canvas/backgrounds/).
144	
145	- With no `backdrop`, there's no copy.
146	- A copy is made only when the framing shows the whole picture somewhere: with `fit`, or with a followed clip that falls back to the whole picture.
147	- If the named track is locked, a matte, or busy over the clip, the copy goes on a new track at the back instead.
148	- A clip with speed actions keeps them on its copy, so the copy shows the same frames.
149	
150	## Written as ordinary edits
151	
152	The framing is written as the clip's position and scale, and one action per move, each of which you can change afterwards like any other [action](/motion/actions/). You'll see them on the [action lane](/motion/action-lane/).
153	
154	**Edit ▸ Undo Reframe Clip** takes the whole framing back in one step, and so does the agent's `undo`.
155	
156	## A clip that already has actions
157	
158	A clip keeps the actions it has. The framing is composed into them, so a zoom or pan the clip already makes still happens, inside the new framing, and a volume or speed action still does what it did.
159	
160	The framing's own moves go in the gaps between the clip's actions. A move that would overlap one is moved up to half a second earlier, or else made part of that action, along its curve.
161	
162	A shot change that falls inside an action cuts the action in three around the one-frame cut. A steady change of volume still sounds exactly as it did, and an eased one eases again on each side of the cut. A speed action, or one a trim left running past the clip's end, is never cut, and takes the framing's change across its length instead.
163	
164	### Start from the whole picture
165	
166	With `replace` set to true, the framing replaces the clip's own moves instead of working inside them. Every position and scale the clip's actions set is removed, the picture is fitted to the canvas, and then the clip is framed. Volume and everything else stay, and an action left with nothing is removed.
167	
168	The default is false. Every kind reads it but `keep` and `layout`. **Clip ▸ Follow Subject…** always starts from the whole picture this way, with a **Backgrounds** track as its `backdrop`, as one undo step named **Follow Subject**.
169	
170	## Which options each kind reads
171	
172	| `follow` | `zoom` | `where_empty` | `backdrop` | `replace` | `from_width`, `from_height` |
173	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
174	| `subject`, `face`, `person`, `salient` | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | No |
175	| `speaker` | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | No |
176	| `cursor` | Yes | No | No | Yes | No |
177	| `center` | Yes | No | No | Yes | No |
178	| `fit` | No | No | Yes | Yes | No |
179	| `layout` | No | No | No | No | Yes |
180	| `keep` | No | No | No | No | Yes |
181	
182	`mics` and `mic_faces` belong to `speaker` alone.
183	
184	## Waiting for analysis
185	
186	If the part of the file the clip plays hasn't been analysed, the tool analyses it and waits up to a minute. It looks at the clip's window with a second either side, for shots, faces and subjects, on your Mac. The answer says whether an analysis ran first.
187	
188	If a minute isn't enough, nothing changes. The answer says which files are still going and how much is covered, and the analysis carries on. The agent asks again to apply the framing.
189	
190	- `center`, `fit` and `keep` need no analysis, and `cursor` and `layout` read none.
191	- `speaker` also needs its microphones' loudness and speech, which Frame Job measures when a file is added.
192	- If the project or the open nest changes while the tool reads the analysis, nothing is framed and the agent is told to call again.
193	- If the analysis fails, nothing is framed and the agent is told which analysis and why.
194	- Stopping the [Assistant](/assistant/chat/) during the wait frames nothing.
195	
196	## When a clip can't be framed
197	
198	A clip that can't be framed is left as it was, and the agent gets a sentence saying why. Frame Job checks in this order and stops at the first one that applies.
199	
200	| The clip | Which kinds it stops | What still works |
201	| --- | --- | --- |
202	| A text, shape, graphic or adjustment clip | All but `keep` | `keep` |
203	| Has no picture, or a crop or scale leaves none | All | Nothing |
204	| A nest clip, then a still or image clip | `subject`, `face`, `person`, `salient`, `cursor`, `speaker` | `center`, `fit`, `keep` |
205	| Its media has no cursor file | `cursor` | `subject`, `center`, `fit`, `keep` |
206	| Its media has a cursor file | `subject`, `face`, `person`, `salient`, `speaker` | `cursor`, `center`, `fit`, `keep` |
207	| On a [matte track](/canvas/matte-tracks/), or cut by a matte | All but `keep` and `layout` | `keep` |
208	| Turned: a rotation, an action turning it, or a spin in its motion | All but `keep` and `layout` | `keep` |
209	| With a copy to make, a nest clip, or a `backdrop` track that isn't behind the clip's | Any kind that makes a copy | Leave `backdrop` out, or name a track further back |
210	| Analysis holds nothing for the part of the clip that plays, or no recorded pointer falls inside it | `subject`, `face`, `person`, `salient`, `cursor` | `center`, `fit`, `keep` |
211	
212	`layout` has [its own checks](#layout), and it skips the matte and turned rows. [`speaker`'s checks](#speaker) come after the turned clip.
213	
214	Before any of that, a call stops on a value it can't use: an unknown clip, track or microphone, or a `from_width` or `from_height` of 0.
215
